recommendation_line: Deliver an internally deleted Becker-type dystrophin by removing exons 54+55 together (in-frame 53|56 junction, −115 aa) using an exon-54-directed PMO that exploits documented human 54+55 coordinated skipping, with a two-PMO 54+55 cocktail as the pre-specified backstop, carried on a TfR1-targeted PMO conjugate for muscle/diaphragm/heart exposure and naked PMO as the fallback format.
recommendation_text: The brief's stated goal is arithmetically dead: the enumeration gives exon 55 = 190 bp, frame remainder 1, so a 54|56 junction frameshifts and the product is another NMD substrate with no cysteine-rich or C-terminal domain. The smallest valid in-frame product containing the lesion is del54-55 (345 bp, Δaa 2625-2739), and it is uniquely favoured because human DMD pre-mRNA already treats exons 54 and 55 as a coupled unit — a published AO directed at exon 54 removes 54+55 together — so the minimum-perturbation product is potentially also a one-oligo product. Verdict is TEST FIRST: the coordinated-skipping ratio is unquantified in everything retrieved, and no human del54-55 or del55-56 carrier phenotype exists, so payload validation must precede any delivery or partnering commitment.
why_this_design: Exon 55 is 190 bp, frame remainder 1: the single-exon skip frameshifts. del54-55 is the smallest in-frame fix, −115 aa, keeping nNOS repeats 16-17 and all of exons 56-79.
Published human coupling (AO to exon 54 removes 54+55) makes the minimal product reachable with one oligo; exons 55-56 have no reported coupling and inherit a full two-skip multiplicative penalty.
Junction fuses 45 aa of repeat 21 to 63 aa of repeat 22 = 108 aa, one canonical repeat length — a hybrid repeat, the configuration linked to milder Becker course.
delivery: Keep payload and delivery strictly separate: exon-54/55 skipping efficiency is unknown for this pair and no number from exon 44, 51 or 53 programs transfers as an expectation. For exposure, the TfR1-conjugate class is the only format with human biopsy-confirmed dystrophin plus animal cardiac restoration, and the tissue list here is explicitly diaphragm- and heart-weighted, which naked PMO does not serve (systemic naked PMO shows poor or absent cardiac dystrophin). Access, not biology, is the constraint: Avidity's AOC platform now sits inside Novartis and Dyne's FORCE is mid-registration and already has an exon-55-directed PMO at IND-enabling stage (DYNE-255), so a partnered or in-licensed conjugate is the realistic route and the exon-55 arm becomes an IP question rather than a discovery one. Build and validate the payload as unconjugated PMO first — commoditised, freedom-to-operate-clean, and sufficient for every mRNA and protein readout — then port the winning sequence(s) onto a TfR1 Fab or mAb conjugate; the TfR1 bicyclic-peptide conjugate is a credible second-generation bet but has no validated PMO-compatible linker. Do not assume CNS reach: no retrieved muscle-optimised conjugate claims it.

backups.concept: Two-PMO cocktail skipping exons 55+56 (54|57 junction, −121 aa)
backups.one_sentence: Co-equal on frame and nearly equal on size with a validated exon-56 oligo (H56A(+92+121)), but it has no reported coordinated skipping, always needs two independent skips in the same transcript, removes essentially all of repeat 22 leaving a 6-aa stub instead of a hybrid repeat, and is the only two-exon option crossing the exon-55/56 boundary beyond which no asymptomatic human in-frame deletion has been reported.

backups.concept: Three-to-four PMO cocktail skipping exons 52-55 (−225 aa)
backups.one_sentence: The only candidate product with a purpose-built in vivo model — a CRISPR Dmd Δ52-55 mouse with WT-level, correctly localised dystrophin and normal muscle and cardiac function at 12 weeks — and it could be three oligos if the exon-54 oligo carries exon 55, but it deletes 110 more residues and the same model loses grip strength and contractile force after exercise at 52 weeks.

critical_risk: The dominant risk is that the exon-54 oligo produces mostly exon-54-only skipped transcript, which joins exon 53 to exon 55 out of frame — converting one NMD substrate into another and potentially lowering whatever residual transcript exists. The single primary source describes exon-54 targeting as giving exon-54-only and exon-54+55 species in roughly comparable amounts, that quantification could not be confirmed from full text, and the patent oligo H54A(+67+97) is described only as giving exon-54 skipping with no mention of exon 55, so coupling is probably oligo- and site-dependent and must be re-measured for every candidate sequence. Second, no human del54-55 carrier phenotype exists in anything retrieved, so protein function rests on frame, domain content and the hybrid-repeat length argument rather than on human genetics. Third, PepGen's result (4.26% skipped transcript, 0.59% dystrophin, program discontinued) proves skipped-mRNA fraction does not predict protein, so this program must be powered on protein. Mitigation: make the ratio of in-frame to out-of-frame product — not total skipping — the primary selection criterion of the ASO walk, and monitor cryptic acceptor use because both published exon-55 oligos sit on the 3' splice site, the configuration most likely to provoke it.

experiment.payload_model: Immortalised or transdifferentiated myotubes from a DMD patient carrying an exon-55 nonsense allele (hemizygous male), with a second independent exon-55-nonsense donor line plus wild-type human myotubes in parallel to read coupling behaviour on an unmutated locus. Delivery at this stage is deliberately artificial — nucleofection or high-dose free uptake of PMO across 0.3–30 µM — because the question is payload behaviour, not exposure.
experiment.payload_constructs: An exon-54 ASO walk of ~20 PMOs tiled across the 3' splice site and the proximal (5') half of the exon, seeded with H54A(+67+97) and Ex54_Ac42 (GAGAAGTTTCAGGGCCAAGTCATTTGCCAC) and biased 5'-proximal per the published PMO-library rule; a parallel exon-55 walk seeded with H55A(-10+20) and Ex55_Ac0 (TCTTCCAAAGCAGCCTCTCGCTCACTCACC); the best exon-54 + best exon-55 pair as a two-oligo cocktail; a brogidirsen-style dual-arm single molecule linking the best exon-54 and exon-55 arms; and for the backup arm the best exon-55 oligo + H56A(+92+121). Controls: scrambled PMO, untreated, and a validated exon-51 PMO as a skipping-competent positive control.
experiment.primary_readout: Long-read or targeted amplicon sequencing across exons 50–60 counting every splice species as a fraction of total DMD transcript — in-frame 53|56, out-of-frame 53|55 (exon-54-only), out-of-frame 54|56 (exon-55-only), any 52/53/56/57 co-skipping, any intra-exonic cryptic junction, intron retention — paired with dystrophin protein by western blot and LC-MS against a quantified normal-muscle standard, and immunofluorescence for dystrophin plus β-sarcoglycan and α-syntrophin to confirm the truncated protein localises and recruits the DGC. Include ± NMD-inhibition arms to separate true splice redirection from differential decay.
experiment.success: At a tolerated dose the in-frame 53|56 species is the dominant skipped product (≥60% of all skipped reads) and reaches ≥20% of total DMD transcript; dystrophin is detectable and concordantly quantified by western and LC-MS with dose-dependence, correct sarcolemmal localisation and DGC recruitment; no single novel cryptic or adjacent-exon junction exceeds 2% of reads; and a single exon-54 oligo achieves this without the exon-55 oligo — if not, the two-oligo cocktail or dual-arm molecule carries forward.
experiment.kill: Kill the one-oligo concept if the best exon-54 oligo yields more out-of-frame exon-54-only transcript than in-frame 53|56 across the whole walk and dose range. Kill the del54-55 product if the two-oligo cocktail also fails to make 53|56 dominant, or if 53|56 transcript is made but no dose-dependent dystrophin is measurable by LC-MS, or if the protein fails to reach the sarcolemma — then move to the 55-56 arm and then 52-55. Nothing advances on an RT-PCR band alone.
experiment.delivery_experiment: Only after a payload wins: conjugate the selected sequence(s) to an anti-TfR1 Fab or mAb and dose humanised hDMD/mdx (or human-TfR1 knock-in) mice and then cynomolgus monkeys intravenously, measuring the 53|56 junction fraction and absolute dystrophin by LC-MS separately in quadriceps, diaphragm and heart, with serum CK plus reticulocyte and renal-tubular safety panels.

precedents.entry: AOs to human dystrophin exon 54 induce transcripts missing exon 54 and exons 54+55 together — the only route to a one-oligo in-frame product here.
Independently restated: directing an AO to human dystrophin exon 54 led to removal of both exons 54+55, citing the all-exon AO panel.
PGN-EDO51 gave 4.26% skipped transcript but 0.59% dystrophin and was discontinued — power this program on protein, never on skipped-mRNA fraction.
Brogidirsen, one PMO product containing two linked sequences against two sites, has 5-year clinical data — a multi-sequence product is developable and regulable.
Dyne DYNE-255, an exon-55-directed PMO on a TfR1-Fab conjugate, is already IND-enabling — the exon-55 arm is a licensing/IP question, not discovery.

lead.therapeutic_product: Mature DMD mRNA with exons 54 and 55 both excluded (exon 53 spliced to exon 56, 345 bp removed, junction ACAGAAACCAAG|GACCTCCAAGGT), translated into an internally deleted Becker-type dystrophin lacking aa 2625-2739 but retaining the N-terminal actin-binding CH1/CH2 domains, the nNOSμ-binding spectrin repeats 16-17, hinge 3, repeats 23-24, and the WW/ZZ/cysteine-rich and C-terminal syntrophin-dystrobrevin modules that anchor the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex at the sarcolemma.
lead.aso_design: Primary design is a single PMO directed at exon 54 — an ASO walk across the exon-54 3' splice site and proximal 5' exonic region, seeded with H54A(+67+97) and Ex54_Ac42 — selected on the ratio of in-frame 53|56 product to out-of-frame exon-54-only product rather than on total skipping. Pre-specified backstops run inside the same screen: a two-PMO cocktail of the best exon-54 oligo plus an exon-55 acceptor oligo (Ex55_Ac0 or H55A(-10+20)), and a brogidirsen-style dual-arm single molecule carrying linked exon-54 and exon-55 sequences, which keeps one drug substance if coupling is only partial.
lead.delivery_strategy: Validate the payload as unconjugated PMO, then port the winning sequence onto an anti-TfR1 PMO conjugate (Fab or mAb) for the clinical asset, since that class alone has human biopsy-confirmed dystrophin plus animal cardiac restoration and Q4W–Q6W dosing; both leading platforms are partner-dependent (Novartis/Avidity, Dyne), so secure access in parallel with payload work. Unconjugated PMO or a stereopure PN backbone is the fallback format if no conjugate access is obtained, accepting that the heart is then essentially untreated.
lead.reason_it_wins: It is the smallest in-frame correction of the lesion — fewest exons and fewest amino acids deleted of any valid block — it is the only block whose two exons are a documented coupled splicing unit in human pre-mRNA so it can plausibly be achieved with one oligo, its junction reconstructs a single canonical-length hybrid spectrin repeat rather than a fractional stub, and it stays entirely upstream of exon 56, the boundary beyond which no asymptomatic human in-frame deletion has been reported, while retaining the nNOS-binding repeats that the much larger 45-55 skip sacrifices.
lead.dominant_risk: That an exon-54-directed oligo yields predominantly out-of-frame exon-54-only skipping, turning one NMD substrate into another — compounded by the absence of any human del54-55 carrier phenotype, so protein function is inferred from frame, domain content and junction geometry rather than observed in a person.

all_candidates.concept: Single exon 55 skip (54|56 junction) — the brief's stated goal
all_candidates.reason: Enumeration is decisive: 190 bp, frame remainder 1, so the junction frameshifts; the product terminates inside spectrin repeat 21 with no WW/ZZ/cysteine-rich or C-terminal domain and is itself an NMD substrate. The brief's own fallback condition is triggered.

all_candidates.concept: Double skip exons 54-55 via a single exon-54-directed PMO exploiting documented 54+55 coupling (53|56 junction, −115 aa)
all_candidates.reason: Smallest in-frame block containing the lesion; the only block with published single-AO coordinated skipping of both its exons; 108-aa hybrid-repeat junction; keeps nNOS repeats and all of exons 56-79; stops at the exon-55 boundary. Coupling ratio unverified, hence TEST FIRST.

all_candidates.concept: Double skip exons 54-55 via two-PMO cocktail (exon-54 ESE oligo + exon-55 acceptor oligo)
all_candidates.reason: Same product and the pre-specified backstop inside the lead experiment if coupling is partial; both oligos have published starting sequences. Costs a second drug substance and makes yield multiplicative.

all_candidates.concept: Double skip exons 54-55 via brogidirsen-style dual-arm single molecule
all_candidates.reason: Preserves a single drug substance while forcing both skips; architecturally precedented by a clinical dual-sequence PMO, but that linked design is Nippon Shinyaku IP needing freedom-to-operate review and there is no DMD multi-exon dual-arm precedent.

Co-equal on frame and nearly equal on size with a validated exon-56 oligo, but no coordinated skipping reported for this pair, it removes essentially all of repeat 22 leaving a 6-aa stub rather than a hybrid repeat, and it is the only two-exon option entering the exon 56-79 region where human benign deletions stop.

all_candidates.concept: Four-exon skip 52-55 (−225 aa) as a 3-4 PMO cocktail
all_candidates.reason: Best product-level in vivo evidence in the set — CRISPR Dmd Δ52-55 mouse with WT-level correctly localised dystrophin and normal function at 12 weeks — and possibly three oligos if exon-54 targeting carries exon 55; but it deletes 110 more residues and the same mouse shows exercise-stress decrement at 52 weeks.

Has the only genuinely asymptomatic adult human carrier in the set (35-year-old male, normal CK 198 IU/L) and retains the nNOS-binding repeats that 45-55 loses, but needs up to eight oligos — unbuildable as a lead for a single exon-55 PTC. Keep as the human-genetics reference point.

Human-anchored only by containment within the benign 45-55/48-55 intervals and the late-cardiomyopathy signature of hinge-3 rod deletions; up to six oligos and an awkward oversized 145-aa junction element for no advantage over 52-55.

all_candidates.concept: Eleven-exon skip 45-55 as a 5-6 PMO cocktail
all_candidates.reason: Unmatched human genotype-phenotype evidence (~90% of del45-55 carriers are BMD, 75/83) and the richest ASO precedent, but it deletes the most protein, loses the nNOSμ-binding site whose cytosolic mislocalisation tracks with worse phenotype, and needs 5-6 oligos — all unnecessary for a single exon-55 PTC. No clinical-stage cocktail program found.

No size advantage over 52-55, deletes two extra exons inside the exon 56-79 interval human genetics flags as intolerant, gives an oversized 126-aa junction element, and has no ASO efficiency data for exons 56 or 57.
Strictly dominated by 52-55: same upstream breakpoint, 110 more residues removed, and it crosses into the exon 56-79 region.
Both remove three of the four repeats immediately upstream of the WW/cysteine-rich anchor and lie wholly inside the exon 56-79 interval where no benign human in-frame deletion exists.

all_candidates.concept: Partial exon 55 removal via an exon-internal cryptic splice site
all_candidates.reason: Contingent on an unverified cryptic acceptor or donor at a frame-compatible distance from the PTC; nothing retrieved maps one. Worse, both published exon-55 oligos sit on the 3' splice site, the configuration that provokes cryptic use — so this is an off-target readout to exclude, not a mechanism to pursue.

all_candidates.concept: NMD evasion / stabilising the exon-55 PTC transcript
all_candidates.reason: Yields more of a rod-domain truncate that cannot bind β-dystroglycan or anchor the DGC, and ASOs cannot induce readthrough. Drop from the program rather than carry as a backup.

all_candidates.concept: Output-raising mechanisms: poison-exon block, 5'UTR/uORF or 3'UTR modulation, antagoNAT transcriptional upregulation
all_candidates.reason: All amplify a message that still carries the exon-55 stop codon; no DMD poison exon, repressive uORF or repressive natural antisense transcript was retrieved. Wrong axis for a nonsense lesion.

all_candidates.concept: Transcript or allele knockdown (RNase H gapmer, allele-selective against the SNV)
all_candidates.reason: Actively harmful in a hemizygous male — there is no second allele to spare and degradation removes rather than restores function.

all_candidates.concept: Surrogate-gene upregulation by ASO (UTRN or disease-modifier transcripts)
all_candidates.reason: Genuinely mutation-agnostic and independent of the PTC, so legitimate as a later combination arm, but no druggable repressive element in UTRN was located in any retrieval and the achievable fold-change and mechanical benefit are unestablished. Unlocated, not excluded.

all_candidates.concept: Nonsense-specific base editing (PBGENE-DMD, single-vector ABE) as the competing mechanism
all_candidates.reason: Not an ASO option but the direct competitor for this exact lesion class, restoring full-length dystrophin in one dose; the live AAV safety crisis in DMD gene therapy and the reversibility of chronic dosing are the ASO program's counter-arguments. Monitor, do not build.
